annotations.text: Engagement Home, Gate 5 direction options. Static mockups, not clickable. doTERRA content is sample data; Train, Deploy and Continuous Support dates are illustrative. All three share the Karta design system, the seven-stage journey with parallel workstreams, a next control point, deliverable states, an attention list, evidence and decisions, Ask this project labelled Beta, and a route to the catalog by stage and readiness. They differ in what leads.

Option A · Journey first
Motivation: the lifecycle is the organizing model, so the dated journey with its parallel lanes is the first thing the eye lands on, then the current stage, then the attention rail. Closest to today's console, lowest change for pilot users.
Trade-off: the next control point sits below the fold on smaller screens, and the journey band spends a lot of height on stages that are months away.

Option B · Control point first
Motivation: the ten control gates in the inventory become the spine. One large card carries the current stage, its objective, the next gate with evidence readiness, deliverable states and two actions; the journey shrinks to a dated strip inside it. Attention, evidence and Ask sit in three equal columns.
Trade-off: Ask this project is one column among three rather than a hero, and the compact strip shows parallel workstreams only as text.

Option C · Ask first
Motivation: you asked to bring Ask this project forward. Here it is the hero with suggested questions, framed as the way into the project's memory. The journey strip and the Now panel follow, attention on the right.
Trade-off: leads with a Beta capability whose answers today come from task data only, and it reads more like a chat product than a delivery workspace. Strongest once Project Chat is grounded in the approved record.
Option A in charcoal. Same hierarchy, density, status language and interaction model as the light version; neutral charcoal surfaces with the lifted Salem accent, never navy.
